S07.title: The Shared Kitchen. Nick and the Pasta Disaster

paragraphs.S07.C000.P000: After the trail, they drove to the guesthouse in Hveragerði and carried in their things. Eric confirmed that they would stay here for both nights. In the evening, Nick announced that he was making pasta. Eric asked whether he knew how. Nick said that it had worked once.

S07.C001.title: If Alice helped Nick with a new shot in S05-C1

paragraphs.S07.C001.P000: Before they went into the kitchen, Nick showed her a few seconds of the wet sleeves he had filmed that morning. There were no faces; in the last shot, he could not get the case closed with his frozen fingers.
paragraphs.S07.C001.P001: “I'll keep this,” he said. “If you don't mind.”
paragraphs.S07.C001.P003: He kept the footage and put away the phone.

S07.C002.title: If Alice rode with Nick in S01-C1

paragraphs.S07.C002.P000: In the kitchen, Nick silently cleared a place for her by the stove. Alice remembered the hour on the road when he had first stopped performing for an audience, and did not push him toward another joke.

paragraphs.S07.C003.P000: Ten minutes later, the water had boiled over onto the stove, the sauce was too spicy, and the colander was a decorative bowl with coin-sized holes.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P001: “Don't touch it,” Nick said when Alice reached for the pot. “The dish has a vision.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P003: “Don't get in the way of art making a mistake.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P004: Alice took the wooden spoon from him.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P005: “Art can make a mistake. Dinner can't.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P006: “That's why I film instead of getting married.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P007: The phrase came out easily, but Nick fell silent for a second afterward. Alice raised an eyebrow.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P008: “Is this an invitation to discuss your biography?”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P009: “It's an attempt to get the spoon back.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P011: He stood beside her and looked into the pot. His shoulder touched hers. Nick did not move away at once, but he did not press either, leaving her room to decide. Alice kept stirring the sauce.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P014: “You already put Icelandic hot sauce and honey in it. It's too late to defend Italy now.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P015: They tasted it. It became edible.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P017: “I saved Eric from having to find a new group.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P021: Nick turned on music on his phone and began moving between the table and the stove with the exaggerated grace of a waiter. He presented Alice's plate on a bent arm.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P022: “Your table, with a view of the coat dryer.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P024: “The window is occupied by the wind.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P025: She took the plate. Nick served the next one to Damir, who had returned from a phone call, and did not ask what it had been about. Eric got the largest portion.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P029: “No. I've admitted that you can ruin my breakfast if you stay hungry.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P030: Over dinner, Nick asked what each of them would refuse to film or describe. Eric said he would not take people onto a closed trail for the sake of a beautiful shot. Damir did not want to tell patients' stories. Alice remembered an interview she had once left out of an article: the subject had spoken without realizing the recording was still running.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P032: He turned his fork in his fingers.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P033: “A person who asked me to turn off the camera.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P036: “Even if it was the best shot of your life?”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P037: “Especially then. Otherwise it isn't the best because I filmed well.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P038: For a second, Nick became completely serious. Then he tasted the pasta and started coughing from the pepper.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P039: “See?” Alice said. “The universe doesn't like beautiful statements.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P042: After dinner, the rain grew heavier. Water drummed on the metal windowsill, and the conversation gradually sank into the steady noise. Nick cleared the plates, set a timer on his phone, and announced:
paragraphs.S07.C003.P043: “We have twenty minutes before Eric sends everyone to bed for safety reasons.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P044: “I don't send anyone to bed,” Eric said.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P045: “Even worse. You let us experience the consequences ourselves.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P048: “A card game. No questions about childhood, trauma, or the meaning of life. Just normal things.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P049: “Do you have normal things?” Alice asked.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P051: “Red card: choose a song for someone tomorrow. Black: assign a small task. Ace: you can refuse.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P052: “You can only refuse on an ace?” Eric asked.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P053: “You can always refuse. On an ace, it's dramatic.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P054: Alice drew first. An eight of hearts.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P056: She looked at the three of them. Damir knew almost all of her old music. Nick deserved something unbearably slow. Eric had been in charge of the road all day and probably expected silence.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P057: “Eric,” she decided. “Tomorrow you'll play a song impossible to plan a route to.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P060: Eric drew the queen of clubs.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P061: “Task for Alice: don't write anything down for ten minutes in the morning.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P068: Damir drew a red card. He chose Nick.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P072: “First, that was an acoustic rehearsal. Second, you lived two rooms away.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P074: Nick drew the king of spades and assigned Damir the task of choosing the worst bun in the bakery in the morning without asking what was in it.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P079: In the second round, Alice drew an ace. She put it on the table.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P081: “But no one has offered you anything yet,” Nick pointed out.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P084: Damir looked at the card, but not at Alice. Eric shuffled the remaining deck.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P085: “You can keep the ace,” he said. “For when you need it.”
paragraphs.S07.C003.P088: Alice slipped the card into her shirt pocket. It was a small thing, but she liked the idea of a visible right to refuse that did not need to be explained.
paragraphs.S07.C003.P089: The next card sent Eric to choose Nick's hat for the next day. Nick demanded “something that doesn't kill the charisma.” Eric brought a bright yellow knitted hat from the hall, forgotten on the guesthouse's hook.

S07.C004.title: If Alice allowed a short recording in S04-C1

paragraphs.S07.C004.P000: Nick reminded her that the shot from the viewpoint was kept only by him, and asked whether he could show it to the others at the table. Alice agreed after watching the trimmed recording once more.

S07.C005.title: If Alice refused to be filmed in S04-C1

paragraphs.S07.C005.P000: Nick did not take out his camera. When Alice raised her phone herself, he looked at her in surprise.
paragraphs.S07.C005.P001: “This is different,” she said. “I want this particular picture.”

S07.C006.title: If Alice suggested a group photo in S04-C1

paragraphs.S07.C006.P000: Nick had already sent all four of them the picture from the viewpoint. Alice found it on her phone and showed Eric how awkwardly he had bent down to make it into the timer shot. Eric asked her not to delete it.

paragraphs.S07.C007.P000: Alice took a picture of Nick on her phone. He struck a pose, then pointed at the camera:
paragraphs.S07.C007.P001: “This is for the private archive only.”
paragraphs.S07.C007.P005: He stepped closer to see the picture. Their heads almost touched. On the screen, Nick looked ridiculous and happy.
paragraphs.S07.C007.P007: Eric watched them across the table without hiding his curiosity, but when Alice looked up, he occupied himself with the cards. Damir folded the towel carefully and went out for another one, though the table was already dry.
paragraphs.S07.C007.P008: The game ended not when the timer went off, but when the owner asked them to keep their voices down. In the hallway, Nick returned the yellow hat to its hook.
paragraphs.S07.C007.P010: “If Eric brings it to the car himself.”
paragraphs.S07.C007.P011: In the morning, the hat was on the passenger seat with a note: “Signal equipment.”

S07.C008.title: Choice S07-C1 — what Alice will keep in the shared archive

S07.C009.title: A. Nick's picture at the table (`kitchenArchive=nick`)

paragraphs.S07.C009.P000: Alice sent the picture only to Nick and added: “Consent check: you decide whether to keep it.” Nick replied that he would keep it, but asked her not to sign it with his name. Later, he returned the yellow-hat picture to her—with her permission this time.

S07.C010.title: B. A group shot with the timer (`kitchenArchive=group`)

paragraphs.S07.C010.P000: Alice suggested putting the phone on the shelf and taking a picture of all four of them. Eric checked that no one else's belongings were in the frame, Damir asked the owner, and Nick set the timer. The picture came out crooked, but no one became an invisible background.

paragraphs.S07.C011.P000: Alice put away her phone. Nick nodded without a joke: “Sometimes a good moment doesn't have to become a file.” In her notebook, she wrote a single line—for herself, not for the article.

paragraphs.S07.C012.P000: The next day, Nick remembered her decision and asked permission before he raised the camera. The small rule proved more useful than any caption: Alice now knew she could change the shape of closeness without disappearing from the conversation.

paragraphs.S07.C013.P000: When Eric came to the kitchen, he asked Alice whether she had noticed anything else interesting on that quiet side of the trail. Nick demanded to know what secret view they had found without him.

paragraphs.S07.C014.P000: In the kitchen, Eric quietly reminded Alice of the song's name. Nick wanted to play it right away, but Alice suggested they finish dinner first.
